short: Gaul, Britain and Spain broke away under a rival line of emperors that Rome could not suppress for fourteen years.
full:
In 260 CE, with Valerian captured and the Rhine frontier collapsing under barbarian raids, the general Postumus rebelled against Gallienus and established a separate empire covering Gaul, Britain, Germania and briefly Spain, with its own consuls, senate and mint at Cologne and Trier. Postumus governed competently and repelled further Rhine incursions, but he was murdered by his own troops in 269 after refusing to let them sack a rebellious garrison town.

His successors, including Victorinus and finally Tetricus, held the breakaway state together through further usurpations and unrest as it steadily lost ground. In 274, Tetricus surrendered to the emperor Aurelian, reportedly by prior arrangement, and the Gallic provinces were reincorporated into a reunified empire after fourteen years of separate rule.
